Work in the git worktree at /opt/nxeon-wip-staff-platform (branch feature/staff-platform, off the Nxeon production repo at /opt/nxeon — do NOT touch /opt/nxeon or /opt/nxeon-staging, only this worktree). Node modules are already installed there (real `npm install`, not a symlink).

This worktree now has Phases 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 7 of a larger staff-platform plan landed and verified (`npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` with `DATABASE_URL="postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/dummy"` currently passes cleanly — confirm this yourself before you start, and again when you're done). Read the full plan first: /root/.claude/plans/validated-napping-possum.md, especially its "Phase 5" section.

Also read, in full, before writing any code:
- `/opt/nxeon-wip-staff-platform/lib/staff-grants.ts` — has `requireAreaOrGrant`, `GRANTABLE_AREAS` (each entry already has the exact `/staff/...` href you need to create).
- `/opt/nxeon-wip-staff-platform/app/staff/layout.tsx` — the employee-portal shell (just landed) — read it to understand how it renders children, so your new pages compose correctly inside it.
- `/opt/nxeon-wip-staff-platform/app/staff/tasks/page.tsx` (already built, part of a different phase) — this is your reference example for the exact "thin staff-portal page" pattern already established in this branch: read it and match its shape/style for the five pages you're building.

## Your job: Phase 5 — wire the six granted tools into `/staff/*` (five real routes + one brand-new one)

For each of these five EXISTING admin tools, the admin-side page already works (gated via `requireAreaOrGrant` from Phase 2) — your job is to extract the page body into a shared, chrome-agnostic component so BOTH `/admin/...` and a new `/staff/...` route render the identical real feature, sharing one implementation:

1. **Support tickets**: `app/admin/support/page.tsx` (list) + `app/admin/support/[id]/page.tsx` (thread) → extract into `components/admin/SupportDeskView.tsx` (list) and a detail-view component of your choosing (name it clearly, e.g. `SupportTicketView.tsx`). New `app/staff/support/page.tsx` and `app/staff/support/[id]/page.tsx`, each `requireAreaOrGrant("supportTickets")` then rendering the shared component(s). Also wire in the `CannedReplyPicker` — read `/opt/nxeon-wip-staff-platform/lib/actions-canned-replies.ts` (already built) and the ticket reply form (find it — likely `ReplyForm` somewhere under `components/`) to add a snippet-picker affordance to the reply textarea (a simple dropdown/button that inserts a canned reply's body into the textarea — don't overengineer this, a `<select>` that appends to the textarea value on change is enough for v1).

2. **Live chat**: `app/admin/chat/page.tsx` → extract its body similarly, new `app/staff/chat/page.tsx` with `requireAreaOrGrant("liveChat")`. Wire the same `CannedReplyPicker` into whatever the chat reply input component is.

3. **Reddit templates**: `app/admin/reddit/page.tsx` → it's thin already (delegates to `components/admin/RedditClient.tsx`); a light duplicate is fine here given how small it is. New `app/staff/reddit/page.tsx`, `requireAreaOrGrant("redditTemplates")`, reusing `RedditClient` directly (it's already a self-contained client component — check whether it takes props requiring an admin-only capability; if it does, verify a granted EMPLOYEE using it is safe, since the underlying actions in `lib/actions-reddit-templates.ts` are already `requireGrant("redditTemplates")`-gated from Phase 2).

4. **Company inbox**: `app/admin/inbox/page.tsx` → extract into `components/admin/CompanyInboxView.tsx`. New `app/staff/inbox/page.tsx`, `requireAreaOrGrant("companyInbox")`.

5. **Company mailboxes**: `app/admin/mailboxes/page.tsx` → reuse `components/admin/CompanyMailboxes.tsx` directly if it's already self-contained (check first). New `app/staff/mailboxes/page.tsx`, `requireAreaOrGrant("companyMailboxes")`.

6. **NEW minimal Clients view — build this fresh, it does not exist anywhere yet, and it is the single most security-critical file in this entire plan:**
   - New `app/staff/clients/page.tsx`, gated `requireAreaOrGrant("clientsBasic")`.
   - Its Prisma query MUST `select` ONLY: `id`, `name`, `email`, `createdAt`, plus `_count: { select: { tickets: true, servers: true } }` on the `User` model (both `tickets: Ticket[]` and `servers: Server[]` are real, already-existing relations — confirm their exact names by reading the `User` model in `/opt/nxeon-wip-staff-platform/prisma/schema.prisma` before writing the query). Absolutely NO `balanceCents`, no `WalletTransaction`/`Invoice` joins, no IP/geolocation data (no `Visit` relation), no `AuditLog` relation, no `CustomerNote` relation, and render NOTHING resembling an impersonate/suspend/credit action anywhere in the component tree. This is not a stripped-down UI on top of a broad query — the SERVER QUERY ITSELF must never fetch the sensitive fields, full stop, per this codebase's own stated principle (quoted in `app/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx`'s comments): "a control a role cannot use is not a permission, it is a promise the server refuses to keep."
   - New shared component `components/staff/ClientsBasicView.tsx` (a simple table: name, email, signup date, ticket count, server count — no per-row action buttons at all, this is read-only).
   - Also add a thin ADMIN-only preview at `app/admin/clients-basic/page.tsx` (`requireArea("platform")`, imported from `@/lib/rbac` — NOT `staff-grants`, since this preview route itself should stay ADMIN-only even though the underlying `clientsBasic` area could theoretically be granted) rendering the identical `ClientsBasicView` component, so the owner can see exactly what a granted employee would see before turning it on for anyone. Note: `"/admin/clients-basic": "clientsBasic"` is ALREADY in `lib/rbac.ts`'s `HREF_AREA` map from an earlier phase — just use `requireArea("platform")` directly for this specific admin preview page regardless of that mapping (the mapping exists for the `/staff` route's grant check, not this preview).

## Constraints
- Verify with `DATABASE_URL="postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/dummy" npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` (no real database in this worktree). Do NOT run `npm run build` or start any server.
- This worktree has been actively edited by multiple parallel agents across several phases — before you start, run `git status` and `git diff --stat main` to see the FULL current state, and read any file you're about to extract/modify fresh (don't rely on descriptions above being byte-exact, the ground truth is what's actually on disk right now).
- Do not touch `app/admin/staff/**`, `lib/actions-staff.ts`, `lib/actions-work.ts`, `components/work/**`, `app/staff/layout.tsx`, `lib/staff-ip.ts` — all already built by other phases. Stay in your lane: the specific files named above for each of the six tools.
- Real production code, no placeholders. The `clientsBasic` query in particular needs to be exactly right — re-read it after writing it and confirm by eye that it could not possibly leak a sensitive field, since this is the one part of the whole plan explicitly built to prevent a new hire from seeing financial/IP/audit data they have no reason to see.
- Match the codebase's existing comment discipline (WHY not WHAT).

## When done
Report: exact files created/modified, confirmation `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` passes cleanly, and — critically — paste the EXACT Prisma `select`/`include` clause you used for the clientsBasic query, so it can be reviewed line-by-line before this ever reaches a real employee.

**The clientsBasic query** (identical in both `app/staff/clients/page.tsx` and `app/admin/clients-basic/page.tsx`):
```ts
const clients = await db.user.findMany({
  select: {
    id: true,
    name: true,
    email: true,
    createdAt: true,
    _count: { select: { tickets: true, servers: true } },
  },
  orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" },
  take: 200,
});
```
No `balanceCents`, no wallet/invoice relation, no `Visit`/IP data, no `AuditLog`, no `CustomerNote` — none of those fields are fetched, so `ClientsBasicView` (a plain 5-column read-only table: name, email, signup date, ticket count, server count) has nothing sensitive available to render even by mistake. The admin preview at `/admin/clients-basic` runs the byte-identical select/component pair.
